html:
The ambush in which Francisco Pizarro and about 170 Spaniards seized the Inca ruler Atahualpa in the town square of Cajamarca, in the northern Andes, on 16 November 1532.

Atahualpa had just won a civil war against his brother Huáscar for the throne of the Inca Empire. He came to meet the strangers with thousands of attendants, most of them unarmed. A Spanish friar handed him a prayer book and called on him to accept Christianity and the Spanish king. Atahualpa threw the book down. The Spanish, hidden around the square, attacked with guns, cannon and horses and killed thousands of people without losing a man.

Atahualpa offered to fill a large room once with gold and twice with silver to buy his freedom. The ransom was paid, but the Spanish executed him in July 1533. They then marched on Cusco and installed a puppet ruler. Disease and the civil war had already weakened the empire, and Cajamarca broke its centre.
sum: The ambush in which Francisco Pizarro and about 170 Spaniards seized the Inca ruler Atahualpa in the town square of Cajamarca, in the northern Andes, on 16 November 1532.
